D9.mechanism_reproduced_from_pinned_source: Fixed-size DHandleEntryTxRx ingress is copied as a struct; MakeSessionByReplyMessage validates registered stub and serviceName length/NUL consistency, then copies DeviceIdInfo without validating NUL termination of fromDeviceId/toDeviceId. A later GET_PROTO_INFO ProcessProto passes these arrays to MessageParcel::WriteString.
source_refs: IPC dbinder_remote_listener.cpp:99-122 (fixed-size ingress and struct copy; socket argument is logged, not carried into message)
IPC dbinder_service.cpp:1113-1122 (raw DeviceIdInfo copy), 1136-1196 (stub/name gates and session attach)
IPC dbinder_service_stub.cpp:107-149 (GET_PROTO_INFO strings written from session fields)
IPC dbinder/c/include/dbinder_types.h (DeviceIdInfo arrays are DEVICEID_LENGTH+1; DHandleEntryTxRx contains following stub/service fields; SessionInfo embeds DeviceIdInfo before stub)

AEAD_and_attacker_boundary.off_path_tampering: For the reviewed ordinary non-AUTH proxy data-channel path, D66 pins source evidence that packets are AES-GCM authenticated/decrypted before session listener delivery. This refutes treating arbitrary off-path packet modification as demonstrated on that route.
AEAD_and_attacker_boundary.valid_key_endpoint: AEAD provides integrity against parties without the session key; it does not stop an authenticated endpoint possessing the key from creating its own valid application payload. That endpoint capability is conditional on actually opening/reaching the relevant DBinder session and the target threat model permitting that peer.
AEAD_and_attacker_boundary.route_binding: The exact DBinder deployment route/channel configuration is not proven to be this proxy path; do not generalize the proxy guarantee to unreviewed channel types.

peer_identity_and_replay.peer_name: D64/D66 trace SRC_BUS_NAME/peerSessionName through auth/session metadata and to PeerSocketInfo.name. Reviewed CheckUidAndPid is a local caller versus local registered-session check; no reviewed branch compares remote name UID/PID to authenticated remote OS credentials. Conversely, this absence does not prove an unauthenticated actor can choose the name: the whole session-open path/permissions remain unbound.
peer_identity_and_replay.replay_freshness: D66 traces proxy decrypt using PacketHead.seq but finds no duplicate/freshness check in the reviewed receive-to-listener chain. No source evidence here proves replay acceptance or rejection for the exact DBinder route; a valid endpoint may also create new valid frames, distinct from replay.

out_of_bounds_and_recipient_challenge.array_boundary: The defect is definitely a missing terminator validation at a fixed char-array boundary (subobject overread risk). DeviceIdInfo is embedded in both DHandleEntryTxRx and SessionInfo, with following members/padding in the enclosing struct; a read beyond one array is not automatically a read beyond the heap allocation. Whether a nonzero following byte string runs past sizeof(SessionInfo), trips ASan, faults, or exposes bytes is unproven.
out_of_bounds_and_recipient_challenge.data_recipient: ProcessProto serializes the values into a MessageParcel reply to the GET_PROTO_INFO caller. The reviewed evidence does not establish which security principal is that caller in the attack path, whether an attacker-controlled peer can receive/read the resulting bytes, or whether any returned bytes are confidential. No reliable confidentiality claim follows.
out_of_bounds_and_recipient_challenge.availability: No reproducible crash or denial effect is established. Layout-only probe is not product evidence.

strongest_counterevidence: Normal request-side string writers use length-aware parcel WriteString and produce terminated fields; this explains compliant traffic but is not receive-side validation.
Reply session requires a registered stub and valid terminated serviceName; malformed stub/serviceName rejects session creation.
The four relevant IPC files match manifest IPC 5903, but no build proof establishes these bytes are in the tested/deployed artifact.
Authenticated proxy endpoint control is not equivalent to arbitrary network/app reachability.
D9.verdict: INSUFFICIENT; retain as a source-bound mechanism/research hypothesis only, not a reportable security candidate. No specific CIA effect or attacker-to-receiver data path is established.
D9.candidate_status: insufficient / parked; no confirmed candidate. Compared with prior evidence, source provenance improved and off-path tamper theory narrowed, but no impact/reachability/build gate changed favorably.

D54_R1.mechanism_reproduced_from_pinned_source: OnRemoteReplyMessage calls MakeSessionByReplyMessage then wakes/detaches by reply.seqNumber. OnRemoteErrorMessage wakes/detaches by reply.seqNumber directly. ThreadLockInfo stores networkId, but lookup/wakeup does not compare it; success session mutation is keyed by reply stub and guarded by registered-stub, serviceName, nonzero stubIndex and attach checks.
source_refs: IPC dbinder_service.cpp:1050-1068 (error/reply dispatch and seq-only wake/detach)
IPC dbinder_service.cpp:1198-1230 (seq-only thread waiter lookup; networkId stored at attach)
IPC dbinder_remote_listener.cpp:99-122 (listener callback does not pass socket identity into parsed message)

AEAD_and_endpoint_capability.off_path_tampering: For the reviewed ordinary proxy path, AES-GCM makes unauthenticated off-path modification unsupported by current source evidence.
AEAD_and_endpoint_capability.valid_key_endpoint: An endpoint holding the session key can construct a valid chosen-sequence payload; authenticated encryption does not constrain application-level sequence fields to the receiver鈥檚 pending request. However D67 finds no evidence that an endpoint on one DBinder session can reach the same listener/context as another peer or target a different peer鈥檚 live waiter.

peer_identity_and_replay.peer_session_name_os_binding: D64/D66 do not establish remote UID/PID binding, but the local CheckUidAndPid semantics and remote-name propagation alone also do not prove a peer can open the privileged DBinder socket. Authentication/device identity is not interchangeable with process identity.
peer_identity_and_replay.replay_freshness: Reviewed proxy receive chain shows authenticated decryption keyed by packet seq but no freshness state at that layer. Exact DBinder route and replay acceptance remain unknown. Replaying a previous valid frame would also need a live matching seq and applicable session/context; these are not demonstrated.

waiter_impact_and_targetability.possible_effect: A mismatched seq can set ready and detach another live waiter; a caller then may observe failed negotiation when querying its own stub鈥檚 missing session. This is a plausible bounded availability effect, not a confidentiality/integrity effect.
waiter_impact_and_targetability.targetability: Process-local uint32 seq allocation is monotonically incremented (wraps), which makes values potentially inferable from a peer鈥檚 own observed requests, but no evidence establishes that a peer can observe adjacent allocations, predict another peer鈥檚 active seq at the needed time, or send to the shared listener across session boundaries.
waiter_impact_and_targetability.preconditions: Requires a valid message accepted by listener, an active waiter with targeted seq, and either same-session malformed response or cross-peer/session reachability. Error sibling has fewer stub/session mutation gates, but still requires the valid SoftBus delivery and live sequence.
waiter_impact_and_targetability.materiality: Single-call negotiation failure may be retryable; no persistent denial, cross-principal action, or product-level availability effect is proven.

strongest_counterevidence: AES-GCM excludes unauthenticated off-path frame forging on the reviewed proxy path.
Success path validates stub and serviceName and requires nonzero stubIndex before attach; invalid success replies need not mutate session state.
Waiter map is process-local and seq-only; source defect is clear, but the attacker鈥檚 cross-session seq acquisition and listener delivery are unproven.
No product-matched integration binary/build or behavioral oracle exists (T65 NO_GO).
D54_R1.verdict: INSUFFICIENT; retain only the existing low-confidence D54-R1 conditional product-verification item, with D55/T56 error handling merged; do not promote or split it.
D54_R1.candidate_status: conditional / insufficient; zero confirmed/reportable candidates. Prior source observation remains; D66 AES-GCM evidence narrows off-path attacker model but does not establish authenticated-peer cross-waiter reachability or security impact.

retained_existing_items: D9 source-bound mechanism, parked as insufficient (not a reportable security candidate)
D54-R1 low-confidence conditional verification item; D55/T56 same root
overall_disposition.candidate_count_interpretation: zero confirmed and zero reportable; D54-R1 is tracked only as a conditional verification hypothesis. D9 is retained in evidence history, not counted as a security candidate until a concrete effect and threat-model reachability are proven.
changes_from_prior_l2: DSoftBus exact source provenance is now verified from the manifest object store; manifest pair is IPC 5903 + DSoftBus 7743, and D9/D54 candidate IPC file bytes match independent anchor bbb92.
Ordinary non-AUTH proxy path source evidence supports AES-GCM integrity before listener delivery, removing support for unauthenticated off-path frame tampering on that path.

No new evidence binds product binaries to this source pair, establishes route selection, anti-replay outcome, remote peer UID/PID principal binding, D9 allocation-boundary escape/data recipient/CIA effect, or D54 cross-peer active-seq targetability.
minimum_evidence_to_reopen: Product build/image provenance tied to manifest IPC 5903 + DSoftBus 7743 and actual DBinder channel route/configuration.
Source/runtime proof whether peer session name and encoded UID/PID bind to authenticated remote process identity and which principals may open/send on the DBinder session.

For D9: exact ASan/bounds oracle showing read past sizeof(SessionInfo) or other concrete fault, plus proof of which security principal receives any bytes and a concrete confidentiality/availability consequence.

For D54-R1: product-matched two-peer test proving a peer can deliver a valid/replayed frame targeting another live waiter鈥檚 seq and produce reproducible availability/integrity effect, with sequence and session controls.
